messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT ir-2025-10-04-267 — regional pin TTL shadowing detected. Metric: regional_misroute_fraction(eu-north1) = 12.7% (baseline 0.2%) starting 3845009900. Several enterprise customers reporting sustained 5xx/timeout for eu-north endpoints. Auto-paging Jules (oncall).

Jules (oncall): ack. Oncall here. Kai/Rafael/Mina — quick summary: is this DNS, routing-policy, or edge pin caching? Any recent deploys to route-annotator or dns-cache?

Kai (netops): initial telemetry: traffic for eu-north1 is being routed to eu-west1 pools for a sustained window (~30m) even though control-plane shows eu-north pinned. Edge decision logs show reuse of cached route decisions beyond expected pin TTLs. Suspect cache TTL source mismatch.

Rafael (dns): I see DNS changes around 3845009400 — we rolled a new authoritative zone for service.redwood.internal with SOA default ttl=86400 as part of infra-dns v5.6.0. That should be fine normally but edge code recently gained a feature to respect DNS TTL as pin TTL when dns-pin-precedence=true.

deploy-bot: deploy event: route-annotator v2.1.0 deployed at 3845009325 -> canary -> 100% at 3845009480. Change: add dns-pin-precedence feature flag + prefer-dns-annotations.

Mina (infra): checking edge logs. Example from eu-edge-21: 
```
[3845009721] route_decision: eu-west1_pool
[reason] cached_pin_from_dns ttl_remaining=84321
[meta] control_plane_pin_ttl=300
```
Edge is honoring dns ttl (24h) over control-plane pin (5m). That explains long-lived misrouting.

Jules (oncall): ok that matches. Mitigation options? Can we flip feature flag off, purge caches, force a control-plane override?

Kai (netops): yes. Plan: 1) set route-annotator feature-flag dns-pin-precedence=false globally 2) push a control-plane emergency override to set explicit pin_ttl=60 for eu-north 3) flush edge decision caches and DNS caches 4) monitor. If that fails, rollback route-annotator to v2.0.8.

Rafael (dns): initiating DNS TTL bump/patch isn't safe (SOA already high). But we can push a DNS record with low TTL for the affected name to force cache eviction: create temporary cname traffic-split-evict.<zone> with TTL=30 and point to same target — edges should refresh. I'll coordinate with Kai to ensure cache flush ordering so we don't create split-brain decisions.

deploy-bot: setting feature-flag route-annotator.dns_pin_precedence=false -> propagating.

Mina (infra): applying control-plane override: 
```
POST /control-plane/overrides
{ "route":"eu-north1", "pin_ttl":"60", "reason":"emergency-evict-3845009999" }
```
Response: 200 OK. Override accepted. Propagation to edge nodes in progress.

Kai (netops): flushing edge decision caches (targeted): 
```
for n in eu-edge-{17..28}; do curl -X POST http://$n/internal/cache/invalidate; done
```
Most nodes 202 Accepted, eu-edge-21 initially timed out — rerun and restarted routing-agent on that node.

Rafael (dns): publishing eviction CNAME: 
```
traffic-split-evict.service.redwood.internal. 30 IN CNAME service.redwood.internal.
```
Propagation started.

(2m)

Mina (infra): edges reporting new pin_ttl=60 applied. Decision logs now show decisions honoring control-plane override. Example: 
```
[3845010045] route_decision: eu-north1_pool
[reason] control_plane_override ttl_remaining=58
```
Telemetry: regional_misroute_fraction dropping from 12.7% -> 1.5% in 3m. p99 latency for eu-north customers improving.

Elena (cs): customers acknowledge update. One customer asked if this will recur; I told them we applied overrides and will follow with RCA. No escalations to legal.

Jules (oncall): good. Keep monitoring 30m. Next steps for RCA: identify why dns-pin-precedence defaulted to true in v2.1.0 and why feature gating didn't trigger a canary metric. Priya please capture product followups.

Priya (product): copying: we need: 1) revert default of dns-pin-precedence to false 2) add unit tests that ensure control_plane_pin_ttl always wins unless explicitly configured 3) add canary guard that watches cross_region_routed_fraction and blocks rollouts that increase it >1% absolute 4) add a runbook step to check authoritative SOA TTLs before enabling dns-based pinning.

Noah (sre): scheduling incident ticket and owners. Also recommend an audit tool to alert when control-plane TTL and authoritative DNS TTL differ more than 10x for any route annotation.

deploy-bot: incident ticket #INC-2025-512 created. assignees: eng-runtime, eng-networking, eng-infra. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2025-512

Kai (netops): telemetry stable. Misroute fraction ~0.4% now. I'll watch for reappearance during next DNS or route-annotator change.

Mina (infra): note for postmortem: root cause appears to be combination of (a) route-annotator v2.1.0 enabling dns-pin-precedence by default and (b) authoritative zone SOA TTL=86400. Edges used dns TTL as pin TTL resulting in long-lived pins that outlived control-plane pin windows. Mitigation performed: feature-flag false, control-plane override, cache flush, dns eviction cname, restart of one node.

Jules (oncall): handing monitoring watch to Noah for 30m. Please escalate on any regression.

Noah (sre): acknowledged. Will monitor and escalate.

incident-bot: ir-2025-10-04-267 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Tags: route-annotator, dns-ttl, pin-ttl, emergency-override.

Priya (product): I'll own the postmortem and coordinate fixes with eng-runtime. Schedule RCA for tomorrow.

Elena (cs): sending targeted customer follow-ups now including timeline and mitigation steps.

Jules (oncall): thanks team. Closing handoff. :white_check_mark:
